config.question: Which testable research directions emerge by mixing artificial-life discovery mechanisms with graph-based materials reasoning?
config.archiveRule: One eligible candidate with highest mean AI-rated rubric score per target × lever cell; ties retain earlier candidate. No novelty score is added to quality.
config.eligibility: At least two distinct known source papers, including one ALife and one Buehler paper; each source use has a locator and explicit transfer boundary; both critics accept niche fit, have no fatal flag, and score grounding >=2. All generated mechanisms remain untested proposals.
config.selection: Two model-generated initial proposals deliberately seeded per cell; one feedback-guided child of each initial elite. This is a small QDAIF-inspired demonstration, not the original QDAIF implementation or an unbiased search-space coverage benchmark.
limitations: Generators, critics and revisers inherit one model family; they are separate contexts, not independent model families.
AI scores express proposal quality under this rubric, not probability of scientific success, novelty certification or empirical validation.
No proposed biological, physical or materials experiment has been executed.
Niches and source cards are human/coordinator designed; targeted initialization makes coverage easier.
Token usage was not measured and no equal-budget superiority claim is made.

candidates.title: Describe deforming motifs by their responses, not their silhouettes

sources.use: Borrow simulation illumination through behavioral representations.
sources.boundary: Representation diversity does not establish physical function.

sources.use: Borrow graph paths as explicit mechanism suggestions.
sources.boundary: Semantic edges do not supply mechanical constants.

candidates.mechanism: Propose positive-stiffness spring motifs. A connectivity-to-deformation graph path selects displacement under two loads as a descriptor. Geometric neighbors become springs, with forces derived from quadratic energy. Archives compare measured responses instead of silhouettes; graph edges never supply mechanical constants.
candidates.hypothesis: Response descriptors may distinguish visually similar motifs with different load transfer, while visual descriptors may separate silhouettes that implement nearly identical responses.
candidates.experiment: On CPU, sample 100 twelve-node motifs and solve fixed-boundary linear equilibria. Build equal-size response and silhouette archives from the identical pool; evaluate withheld load directions.
candidates.baseline: Match motif pools, archive sizes and equilibrium solves for response, silhouette and random archives.
candidates.metric: Report pairwise distances between held-out displacement responses and reconstruction of response classes, alongside occupied bins under a fixed independent evaluator.
candidates.falsifier: Reject the proposed advantage if held-out response separation is no better than random across repeated pools, or follows only node count or stiffness totals.
candidates.confound: Unconstrained rigid modes and overall stiffness can dominate distances; fix boundaries, normalize material budget and report dimensional versus normalized responses.
candidates.feasibility: One-day dimensionless CPU toy using NumPy; physical validation, biological agency and open-ended evolution remain unestablished.

candidates.title: Compile relation graphs into a bounded Lenia kernel grammar

sources.use: Borrow niche archives of continuous cellular patterns.
sources.boundary: This toy does not demonstrate open-ended evolution.

sources.use: Borrow interpretable relational representations for candidate construction.
sources.boundary: Conceptual relations do not determine kernel physics.

candidates.mechanism: Propose a graph grammar for continuous cellular automata. Nodes denote channels; edges compile to normalized radial kernels and bounded growth coefficients. An inhibition relation proposes an edge type, with mathematics independently defined. Compare graph mutations against flat coefficient mutations.
candidates.hypothesis: If reusable motifs provide useful search structure, grammar mutations may retain viable patterns more often than matched flat mutations after a new channel coupling is introduced.
candidates.experiment: Run 60 paired mutations on a 32-by-32 grid for 150 steps, matching starting patterns and parameter ranges; evaluate a withheld seed.
candidates.baseline: Match coefficient counts, mutation norms, rollouts and archive capacities; add a label-shuffled grammar.
candidates.metric: Measure surviving localized patterns after mutation and held-out-seed persistence; report descriptor coverage using one frozen evaluator for every encoding.
candidates.falsifier: Reject a grammar benefit if matched flat encoding performs equally or better, or any apparent gain disappears after matching the distribution of coefficient changes.
candidates.confound: Grammar search may silently restrict candidates to safer regions. Log the induced parameter distribution and compare conditioned subsets before attributing a compositional advantage.
candidates.feasibility: One-day dimensionless CPU toy using NumPy; physical validation, biological agency and open-ended evolution remain unestablished.

candidates.title: Test when nonreciprocal particle couplings produce functional pursuit

sources.use: Borrow typed-particle interaction matrices as a searchable substrate.
sources.boundary: Attraction patterns alone do not establish agency.

sources.use: Borrow paths to propose testable directional relationships.
sources.boundary: A graph arrow is not evidence for a force law.

candidates.mechanism: Propose a two-species overdamped particle toy where a graph path suggests asymmetric sensing. Specify bounded radial interactions a12 and a21; drag removes momentum conservation. Search reciprocal and nonreciprocal families for localized pursuit tracking a displaced resource, rather than task-free circling.
candidates.hypothesis: Under specified drag and resource attraction, asymmetric coefficients may support sustained pursuit with better tracking than reciprocal couplings of the same interaction strength.
candidates.experiment: Simulate 24 particles for 400 steps over 40 coefficient pairs and ten seeds; displace a resource halfway through and measure tracking after the intervention.
candidates.baseline: Match force bounds, drag, seeds and rollouts for reciprocal, asymmetric and species-shuffled controls.
candidates.metric: Use post-displacement resource distance, cluster persistence and speed; include total force magnitude to expose gains purchased by stronger actuation.
candidates.falsifier: Reject the pursuit claim if tracking gains vanish under matched force magnitude or occur equally when the resource displacement signal is removed.
candidates.confound: Circular motion can masquerade as tracking, and boundary wrapping can reduce apparent distances; use unwrapped trajectories and counterfactual resource positions.
candidates.feasibility: One-day dimensionless CPU toy using NumPy; physical validation, biological agency and open-ended evolution remain unestablished.

candidates.title: Couple elastic deformation to a local reaction pattern

sources.use: Borrow persistence and locomotion measures for local patterns.
sources.boundary: A reaction toy is not a Lenia replication.

sources.use: Borrow explicit graph interpretation linked to executable modeling.
sources.boundary: Retrieved analogies do not establish constitutive equations.

candidates.mechanism: Propose an elastic ring carrying an activator-inhibitor field. A strain-to-activation-to-rest-length cycle compiles to explicit equations: strain adds bounded activation, activation changes rest lengths, and positions follow elastic gradients. Declare external chemical drive; graph relations supply dependencies, never unvalidated material constants.
candidates.hypothesis: Within a stable parameter region, two-way coupling may preserve a traveling excitation after a localized mechanical disturbance more often than one-way coupling.
candidates.experiment: Sweep 30 coupling settings, ten seeds and 500 steps; indent one ring node at a fixed time and track pulse propagation and recovery with timestep-halving checks.
candidates.baseline: Match initial fields, elastic budgets and integration calls across two-way, one-way and zero coupling.
candidates.metric: Measure pulse lap completion, recovery time and bounded deformation; report chemical drive and elastic dissipation separately rather than inferring efficiency.
candidates.falsifier: Reject the coupling advantage if it disappears under timestep refinement or if comparable persistence requires no strain feedback.
candidates.confound: Numerical instability and imposed reaction oscillations can mimic self-organization; test isolated field dynamics, boundedness and dependence on initial phase.
candidates.feasibility: One-day dimensionless CPU toy using NumPy; physical validation, biological agency and open-ended evolution remain unestablished.

candidates.title: Give a spring motif a local record of previous loading

sources.use: Borrow trajectory-conditioned searches for dynamical motifs.
sources.boundary: Distinct trajectories do not establish useful memory.

sources.use: Borrow executable constitutive fitting and validation loops.
sources.boundary: The proposed law is not an experimentally fitted material.

candidates.mechanism: Propose spring motifs with slow rest-length variables relaxing toward extension. A loading-history-response path maps to an explicit internal-variable energy with positive relaxation and damping. Search relaxation times for history discrimination while matching geometry and current force; graph analogy establishes no constitutive validity.
candidates.hypothesis: A slow internal variable may preserve information about pulse order after fast displacement relaxes, permitting better discrimination than a memoryless spring motif.
candidates.experiment: Apply AB and BA load pulses with equal total impulse; after a fixed delay, apply the same probe and classify histories using displacement in 100 noisy repeats.
candidates.baseline: Use frozen-memory and randomized-history controls; match geometry, stiffness, pulse energy and classifier data.
candidates.metric: Report held-out history classification, decay with delay and dissipated work; test whether separation survives conditioning on the visible pre-probe geometry.
candidates.falsifier: Reject hidden-memory behavior if classification falls to chance after geometry matching, or if initial-state leakage predicts history equally well.
candidates.confound: Residual displacement, unequal work and classifier overfitting can mimic memory; split by noisy realization and audit the full mechanical state before probing.
candidates.feasibility: One-day dimensionless CPU toy using NumPy; physical validation, biological agency and open-ended evolution remain unestablished.

candidates.title: Separate refractory-state memory from visible cellular shape

sources.use: Borrow phenotype trajectories and localized-pattern evaluation.
sources.boundary: A latent descriptor does not identify causal memory.

sources.use: Borrow a graph path to formulate a mechanistic hypothesis.
sources.boundary: The graph supplies an experimental suggestion, not proof.

candidates.mechanism: Propose a cellular pattern with refractory channel h integrating activation and inhibiting growth. The activation-to-refractoriness-to-response path maps to h-next=(1-alpha)h+alpha*x plus inhibited growth. Swap or reset h while keeping visible x identical to causally test state-dependent responses rather than infer memory from descriptors.
candidates.hypothesis: If refractory state stores operational history, identical visible patterns should respond differently to an identical probe after h swapping, with differences decaying at the specified relaxation timescale.
candidates.experiment: Use 32-by-32 grids, paired activation pulses and ten seeds; copy visible state across matched histories, then swap hidden channels before applying a fixed probe.
candidates.baseline: Use reset-memory, shuffled-memory and memoryless controls; match grids, rollouts, patterns and probes.
candidates.metric: Measure probe-induced mass change and recovery latency as functions of pulse interval; estimate the causal effect of hidden-channel replacement on matched visible states.
candidates.falsifier: Reject a refractory-memory explanation if hidden-state swaps do not alter response, or differences persist unchanged after resetting h.
candidates.confound: A hidden channel can simply change effective excitability. Compare spatially shuffled and constant-mean h to distinguish local history structure from a scalar gain change.
candidates.feasibility: One-day dimensionless CPU toy using NumPy; physical validation, biological agency and open-ended evolution remain unestablished.

candidates.title: Select locally persistent patterns for recovery across lesion types

sources.use: Borrow local competition in a behavioral archive.
sources.boundary: Archive occupancy does not prove biological adaptability.

sources.use: Borrow structure-function paths to propose intervention families.
sources.boundary: Materials analogies do not certify cellular regeneration.

candidates.mechanism: Propose selecting cellular patterns in mass-speed niches, replacing persistence fitness with lesion recovery. A redundancy-to-connectivity-to-damage-tolerance path proposes central and peripheral erasure. These operators act on cellular state; graph terminology changes no growth equations and asserts no tissue equivalence.
candidates.hypothesis: At equal rollout budget, lesion-conditioned selection may improve recovery to withheld lesion locations compared with selection for undisturbed persistence alone.
candidates.experiment: Mutate 80 candidates around a known viable seed on a 32-by-32 grid. Alternate two training lesion classes; evaluate retained patterns on held-out wedge lesions and seeds.
candidates.baseline: Match mutations, niches and simulation steps; give persistence-only selection extra repeated evaluations.
candidates.metric: Measure post-lesion survival, normalized mass recovery and connected-pattern retention; report undisturbed persistence and occupied niches to expose robustness-diversity tradeoffs.
candidates.falsifier: Reject transferable recovery if gains occur only for trained lesion masks, reflect simply larger initial mass, or disappear on held-out initial conditions.
candidates.confound: Mass and empty-space placement can mechanically reduce lesion severity; match fractional mass removed and analyze size-stratified outcomes.
candidates.feasibility: One-day dimensionless CPU toy using NumPy; physical validation, biological agency and open-ended evolution remain unestablished.

candidates.title: Select visual novelty against intervention-tested function

sources.use: Borrow historical novelty and representation-based illumination.
sources.boundary: A novelty proxy does not establish functional innovation.

sources.use: Borrow interpretable hypotheses checked by executable modeling.
sources.boundary: Graph assertions require an independently specified test.

candidates.mechanism: Propose excitable cellular motifs where graph paths name functions compiled into perturbation assays. Compare visual novelty selection against response novelty conditional on viability. A control renderer adds color cycles without changing state; functional responses are measured on unrendered dynamics, not semantic descriptions.
candidates.hypothesis: Function-conditioned selection may resist color-cycle novelty traps better than visual selection while retaining patterns with distinct responses to local deletion and timed excitation.
candidates.experiment: Evaluate 80 shared candidate rules on 24-by-24 grids with three renderers; build equal-capacity archives and evaluate unselected perturbation times and deletion locations.
candidates.baseline: Match pools, rollouts, assays and archive sizes for visual, response and random selection; count descriptor costs.
candidates.metric: Report renderer sensitivity of archive membership, held-out response diversity and viable fraction; compute function descriptors using fixed lesion and excitation definitions.
candidates.falsifier: Reject the selection advantage if response-selected archives lack more held-out functional diversity than random or are equally altered by renderer-only changes.
candidates.confound: Handcrafted assays privilege chosen functions and may miss meaningful visual dynamics; preserve disagreements rather than declaring visual novelty scientifically worthless.
candidates.feasibility: One-day dimensionless CPU toy using NumPy; physical validation, biological agency and open-ended evolution remain unestablished.

candidates.title: Typed evidence packets for collective hidden-state inference

sources.use: Multiagent information aggregation motivates the collective task.
sources.boundary: No claim of emergent cognition or living agents.

sources.use: Ontological relation paths motivate typed message fields.
sources.boundary: Relation types are an engineering representation, not physical laws.

candidates.mechanism: Eight rule-based agents observe noisy fragments of a hidden binary state. Compare free-form recorded packets with typed packets separating observation, inferred relation and uncertainty. A receiving agent composes only compatible relation paths, preventing repeated hearsay from being counted as fresh observations.
candidates.hypothesis: Typed packets should reduce error more under duplicated reports than independent reports, specifically testing resistance to repeated hearsay.
candidates.experiment: Vary duplication and sensor reliability in matched CPU runs; fix sensor draws, packet capacity and total messages across formats.
candidates.baseline: Compare untyped communication and an equal-budget independent ensemble; equalize observations, packet capacity and final aggregation access.
candidates.metric: Measure decision error, calibration and duplicate-evidence overcount on held-out draws; lexical diversity is never scored as functional diversity.
candidates.falsifier: Reject if untyped packets with identical provenance match accuracy, or gains require greater packet capacity or more sensor samples.
candidates.confound: Compression could explain gains. Pad capacity and separately ablate provenance, relation labels and uncertainty to identify the effective component.
candidates.feasibility: Discrete-event Python and recorded templates suffice; observations are synthetic. This is an unexecuted proposal requiring no language-model runtime.

candidates.title: Collective descriptors that separate coordination from shared drift

sources.use: Trajectory embeddings motivate collective descriptors.
sources.boundary: Embedding novelty is not functional innovation.

sources.use: Interpretable graphs motivate relative-coordinate features.
sources.boundary: Swarm graphs are not materials constitutive models.

candidates.mechanism: Represent simulated foraging populations using encounter graphs and resource-transfer relations, alongside rendered trajectory embeddings. Relative graph features remove uniform translation while retaining coordinated exchange. Archive teams by either descriptor, then evaluate unseen resource layouts with a frozen archive, separating apparent visual novelty from successful transfer strategies.
candidates.hypothesis: Graph descriptors should retain more transfer strategies succeeding after spatial shifts; image descriptors should retain more shifted duplicates.
candidates.experiment: Compare matched descriptor archives in grid-world populations, then replay frozen elites on translated and shuffled-resource maps with identical budgets.
candidates.baseline: Compare handcrafted descriptors and an equal-budget independent ensemble; equalize observations, policy evaluations, simulator steps and embedding computation.
candidates.metric: Measure held-out delivered resources, transfer motifs and translation-equivalent duplicates; embedding distance and niche occupancy do not establish functional diversity.
candidates.falsifier: Reject if image elites match after translated duplicates merge, or graph descriptors erase spatial specialization needed for resource delivery.
candidates.confound: Invariance can erase meaningful position. Include anchored-resource maps and report losses as well as gains across environmental conditions.
candidates.feasibility: CPU grid-worlds and compact graph features suffice; prerecorded image embeddings are possible if their computation is explicitly budgeted.

candidates.title: Contradiction-triggered quorum checks in communicating populations

sources.use: Communication among heterogeneous agents supplies the collective setting.
sources.boundary: Task success does not establish general intelligence.

sources.use: Specialized generation and critique motivate message challenges.
sources.boundary: Critique becomes a testable protocol, not validation of materials claims.

candidates.mechanism: In distributed hazard detection, agents broadcast local observations. A contradiction between two reports activates a critic that requests one fresh sensor sample before a quorum acts. Challenge tokens are limited, so the protocol concentrates interaction on disagreements instead of broadcasting every observation equally.
candidates.hypothesis: Contradiction-triggered sampling should reduce false alarms under localized failures, but lose its advantage under common-mode corruption shared by all sensors.
candidates.experiment: Replay matched sensor draws under localized and shared failures; equalize sampling budgets across challenge, broadcast and independent conditions.
candidates.baseline: Compare random resampling, majority voting and an equal-budget independent ensemble; count challenge messages and every additional sensor sample.
candidates.metric: Measure false alarms, missed hazards, delay and useful observations per message; differing rationales never count as distinct detection functions.
candidates.falsifier: Reject if random resampling matches targeted challenges, or if gains disappear after extra sensor observations and messages are equalized.
candidates.confound: Disagreements may expose sensor identities. Randomize identities, fix failure prevalence and evaluate unseen failure patterns across matched seeds.
candidates.feasibility: Binary sensors, finite-state quorums and prerecorded packets fit a CPU simulator; this proposed experiment needs no physical sensors.

candidates.title: Novelty-guided communication routing through complementary sensors

sources.use: Historical novelty motivates exploring alternative interaction patterns.
sources.boundary: Finite routing novelty does not imply open-ended evolution.

sources.use: Graph-path sampling motivates communication routes.
sources.boundary: Information routing is tested directly; no physical analogy is assumed.

candidates.mechanism: Agents observe different components of a small parity puzzle. Route a limited number of packets along sampled graph paths, rewarding routes that encounter previously uncombined sensor types. Historical route novelty operates on information-source combinations rather than wording, allowing the population to discover complementary communication circuits.
candidates.hypothesis: Source-combination routing should improve parity recovery on sparse networks; gains should shrink when every component is already directly accessible.
candidates.experiment: Evolve route policies across small graphs; test held-out sensor allocations and edge failures using matched puzzles and packet budgets.
candidates.baseline: Compare random walks, centrality routing and an equal-budget independent ensemble; equalize received packets and forbid privileged global sensor access.
candidates.metric: Measure parity accuracy, required-source delivery and resilience after edge removal; route novelty alone never qualifies as functional diversity.
candidates.falsifier: Reject if source-aware random routing matches accuracy, or gains depend on withholding equivalent information from the independent ensemble reducer.
candidates.confound: Source labels may leak puzzle structure. Provide identical metadata everywhere and test puzzles requiring irrelevant sensor components to be ignored.
candidates.feasibility: CPU graph simulation with binary packets and exhaustive small puzzles suffices; count transmissions explicitly, without autonomous language-model calls.

candidates.title: A minority-memory archive for collective adaptation after regime shifts

sources.use: Locally competitive archives motivate retaining multiple strategies.
sources.boundary: Archive occupancy does not establish indefinite innovation.

sources.use: Graph-connected hypotheses motivate indexing collective strategies by relations.
sources.boundary: The indexed objects are policies, not validated materials mechanisms.

candidates.mechanism: A communicating foraging population stores successful coordination policies in a bounded graph-indexed memory. Each niche preserves a minority policy defined by resource-transfer structure, even while the dominant policy earns more current reward. After a resource regime switches, agents retrieve policies matching the new transfer constraints.
candidates.hypothesis: Minority-policy memory should shorten recovery after recurring regime shifts, while producing a measurable stationary-environment cost from reserving archive space.
candidates.experiment: Run recurring, unprecedented and absent regime shifts in matched grid-world seeds; equalize memory slots, retrieval attempts and simulator steps.
candidates.baseline: Compare FIFO, top-reward memories and an equal-budget independent ensemble; equalize total policies retained, retrieval trials and communication counts.
candidates.metric: Measure recovery time, stationary reward cost and successful transfer patterns; different policy descriptions never substitute for distinct behavioral effects.
candidates.falsifier: Reject if reward-only retention matches recovery under equal memory, or benefits occur only on previously memorized resource layouts.
candidates.confound: Archive indices may leak regimes. Use observable encounters and transfers only; test unfamiliar resource placements without privileged regime labels.
candidates.feasibility: Finite-state policies and bounded graph features permit CPU execution; any result would concern synthetic adaptation rather than biological memory.

candidates.title: Provenance memory that limits collective error cascades

sources.use: Multiagent information sharing motivates cascade experiments.
sources.boundary: Social organization is an experimental setting, not evidence of life.

sources.locator: Results and Discussion: retrieval and ontological graphs
sources.use: Retrieved relations motivate source-linked episodic memory.
sources.boundary: Retrieved claims remain defeasible; graph edges are not causal proof.

candidates.mechanism: Agents retain packet ancestry in an episodic graph: original observation, relay chain and later correction. Repeated relays share one evidential weight. When a source is disproved, agents discount descendants while preserving unrelated observations, potentially allowing a communicating population to reverse a mistaken consensus.
candidates.hypothesis: Ancestry memory should accelerate correction after influential-source failure, particularly in clustered networks that repeatedly circulate the same observation.
candidates.experiment: Replay binary reports through graph populations; time a ground-truth correction and vary clustering while matching packets, memory and sensor reliability.
candidates.baseline: Compare timestamp-only memory, flat retrieval and an equal-budget independent ensemble; provide identical corrections, original observations and total storage.
candidates.metric: Measure reversal delay, residual false beliefs and valid-evidence retention; lexical variation across relays does not count as independent evidence.
candidates.falsifier: Reject if flat source-tagged memory matches ancestry tracking, or if ancestry discounting suppresses genuinely independent corroboration enough to negate gains.
candidates.confound: Perfect ancestry is unrealistic. Hide and corrupt links, reporting failure thresholds instead of assuming reliably available provenance in every packet.
candidates.feasibility: CPU packet replay and adjacency lists suffice; all reports are synthetic, and no actual scientific claims or cognition are adjudicated.

candidates.title: Selecting complementary role mixtures instead of individually strong agents

sources.use: Local niche competition motivates a population archive.
sources.boundary: Niches are chosen descriptors, not certified functional categories.

sources.use: Specialized agent roles motivate heterogeneous team composition.
sources.boundary: Role labels alone do not demonstrate complementarity or independence.

candidates.mechanism: Select whole teams in a resource-transport simulation, archiving mixtures of scouts, carriers and signalers by measured interaction patterns. Within each niche, reward delivered resources. Mutations alter role proportions and communication thresholds, allowing individually weak signalers to survive when they improve team coordination.
candidates.hypothesis: Team niche selection should retain useful signalers under sparse discovery; their advantage should diminish when all resources become directly visible.
candidates.experiment: Evolve finite-state teams under sparse visibility, then test dense visibility and role removal with matched mutation opportunities and simulator evaluations.
candidates.baseline: Compare individual selection, reward-only team selection and an equal-budget independent ensemble; equalize sensing, movement, population sizes and evaluation counts.
candidates.metric: Measure delivery reward, losses after signaler removal and successful role mixtures; role names alone do not demonstrate functional diversity.
candidates.falsifier: Reject complementarity if removing signalers changes no reward, or if matched reward-only selection finds equally effective teams at equal budget.
candidates.confound: Signalers may have privileged sensing or cheaper actions. Equalize both, then treat information asymmetry as an explicitly varied experimental factor.
candidates.feasibility: Finite-state grid agents permit CPU search and exact role ablations; this untested proposal makes task-specific predictions about synthetic transport.

candidates.title: Selecting collective policies across communication breakdown niches

sources.use: Diverse targets motivate fault niches.
sources.boundary: Finite coverage is not open-endedness.

sources.use: Simulation connects proposals to executable checks.
sources.boundary: No physical materials claim follows.

candidates.mechanism: Archive consensus policies by tolerance to delay, loss and corrupt relays. Select competitive policies within each fault regime, then assemble mixed populations switching with observed network conditions. Selection retains recovery mechanisms across faults; semantic novelty supplies no reward. Held-out fault sequences test whether specialized policies jointly generalize.
candidates.hypothesis: Niche-selected mixtures should recover consensus after communication-regime switches more reliably than average-reward selection, while causing errors near switching boundaries.
candidates.experiment: Train on separate packet-fault regimes, then test held-out switching sequences; equalize evaluations, messages and network-detector information across conditions.
candidates.baseline: Compare average-reward selection, worst-case selection and an equal-budget independent ensemble; also give homogeneous populations the identical regime detector.
candidates.metric: Measure correct consensus, recovery delay, switching errors and failure-profile coverage; semantic policy differences alone do not establish functional diversity.
candidates.falsifier: Reject if detector-equipped homogeneous policies match recovery, or mixed populations succeed only by transmitting additional packets during regime transitions.
candidates.confound: Detection may supply the benefit. Freeze or scramble detector outputs and disable switching to separate archive, mixture and detector effects.
candidates.feasibility: Deterministic policies and simulated packet faults allow CPU execution; this untested proposal predicts synthetic distributed behavior, not physical materials properties.

candidates.title: Behavioral niches for evidence-retrieval workflows

sources.use: Behavioral niches and local competition.
sources.boundary: No open-endedness guarantee.

sources.use: Ground retrieval and executable mappings.
sources.boundary: Relations require assumption checks.

candidates.mechanism: Encode retrieval traces by evidence type, relation coverage and contradiction handling. Learn training-only descriptors and retain locally competitive workflows across niches. Graph-grounded traces let Lenia-style illumination diversify retrieval behavior rather than answer wording.
candidates.hypothesis: Behavioral niches preserve retrieval strategies useful for different test materials questions, improving worst-question-type performance compared with selecting one globally highest-scoring retriever.
candidates.experiment: Author fifty evidence cards with explicit claims and distractors. Split templates before searching retrieval depth, relation filters and contradiction rules; freeze workflows before testing.
candidates.baseline: Compare random search, global top-k and fixed lexical retrieval using same configurations, evidence access, context limits and scoring-call budgets across matched seeds.
candidates.metric: Predeclare test supported-answer accuracy, citation precision and worst-template accuracy. Report archive coverage separately using fixed categories; descriptor spread is not research quality.
candidates.falsifier: Reject the advantage if worst-template accuracy fails to improve across matched seeds, or if randomly permuted descriptors perform equally well at equal budgets.
candidates.confound: Wording may favor descriptors. Hold out relation families and question templates; match context length so varied contexts cannot simply supply more evidence.
candidates.feasibility: Offline Python retrieval over authored cards runs on CPU. Exact claim keys provide labels; cache optional model paraphrases before any train-test split.

candidates.title: Counterfactual descriptors for graph-guided experiment plans

sources.use: Transfer trajectory novelty to workflow search.
sources.boundary: Novelty is observer dependent.

sources.use: Graph-path hypothesis construction.
sources.boundary: Graph paths do not validate properties.

candidates.mechanism: Encode plans by discrimination among toy spring laws. Graph paths propose measures; nearest-neighbor illumination retains distinct discrimination vectors. ASAL trajectory search becomes workflow search over observable consequences under explicit competing models.
candidates.hypothesis: Counterfactual descriptors retain experiments discriminating different mechanisms, whereas lexical novelty retains differently phrased plans with redundant consequences on test model pairs.
candidates.experiment: Author three spring-network laws and candidate measures. Archive graph-derived plans on training networks, then test frozen selections on withheld networks and hidden laws.
candidates.baseline: Use same plan pools and measure budgets for lexical novelty, random archive assignment and global info selection; freeze descriptor dimensions before holdout evaluation.
candidates.metric: Measure hidden-law identification, redundant measures and cost per correct identification on fixed holdouts. Report descriptor coverage separately from task outcomes and physical validity.
candidates.falsifier: Reject the proposal if discrimination niches do not improve identification or reduce redundancy, or gains disappear when every method receives identical initial plans.
candidates.confound: Correctly specified toy laws exaggerate usefulness. Include a withheld fourth law and unknown-model response; calibration under misspecification matters alongside model identification accuracy.
candidates.feasibility: Small linear spring systems and plan enumeration require only CPU NumPy. Any result concerns a planning benchmark, without validating actual materials or hypotheses.

candidates.title: Compatibility-tested recombination of scientific workflows

sources.use: Behavioral niches and local competition.
sources.boundary: No open-endedness guarantee.

sources.use: Ground retrieval and executable mappings.
sources.boundary: Relations require assumption checks.

candidates.mechanism: Recombine typed retrieval, solver and validation modules across niches only when units, shapes and assumptions align. Execute parents, single substitutions and combined children to measure interactions. Grounded executable mappings constrain Lenia-style variation.
candidates.hypothesis: Compatibility-constrained recombination yields more accurate executable workflows per evaluation than unconstrained crossover; factorial tests reveal individually useful modules that become harmful together.
candidates.experiment: Build spring-network tasks and typed modules containing unit and boundary-condition traps. Search training topologies, then execute selected workflows on unseen topology families.
candidates.baseline: Compare mutation-only, unconstrained crossover and random assembly with equal attempted children, solver calls and validation budgets; charge compatibility screening to total cost.
