candidates.changes: Defined laws, loads, noise, Gaussian descriptor, equivalence classes and unknown calibration; isolated test labels; added independent archive builds and charged descriptor forward solves.

candidates.title: Budget-accounted factorial tests of workflow recombination

sources.use: Behavioral niches and local competition.
sources.boundary: No open-endedness guarantee.

sources.use: Ground retrieval and executable mappings.
sources.boundary: Relations require assumption checks.

candidates.mechanism: Transfer Lenia niche retention to typed workflows with MechGPT-style executable mappings. Modules declare units, shapes, boundary assumptions and pure JSON-to-array interfaces. Recombine two slots: A assembles units/boundaries; B configures the solver. Execute parent 00, substitutions 10 and 01, and combined child 11 on identical problems.
candidates.hypothesis: Assumption-aware compatibility may improve valid workflows per computational cost. Recombination needs to exceed mutation and type filtering; source papers do not establish workflow-crossover synergy.
candidates.experiment: Publish fixed modules and spring generators before search: SI conversion, boundary assembly, linearization and nonlinear bisection. Some modules pass types but violate assumptions. Reserve topology generators and entire assumption-error families. Run twenty independent searches; estimate factorial contrasts within matched withheld problems and noise seeds.
candidates.baseline: Primary budget is 10000 accounting units: type checks 1, assumption checks 2, solver calls 20, archive operations 1. Charge rejected children; freeze weights after training-only timing calibration, reporting wall time and raw counts. Compare no screening, type-only, assumption-aware, mutation-only and random assembly. Auxiliary designs separately fix attempted children or solver calls; neither claims both matched.
candidates.metric: L=displacement RMSE/fixed training displacement scale, clipped at 2; invalid workflows receive L=2. Interaction I=L11-L10-L01+L00 is negative for beneficial nonadditivity. Report all four losses, executable fraction, accuracy per cost and independent-build intervals; bootstrap builds rather than repeated evaluations.
candidates.falsifier: Reject added value if assumption checks do not exceed type-only controls at primary cost, or one substitution explains all improvement without negative interaction. Contrasts depend on loss scale, not universal scientific synergy.
candidates.confound: Curated traps may favor the checker. Withhold error families, include valid unusual modules and report false rejection. Public interface metadata must not expose hidden correctness labels; only specifications and training observations guide checks.
candidates.feasibility: A CPU JSON executor and NumPy solvers suffice. Accounting weights are operational rather than universal compute equivalence; vary them in sensitivity analyses. This remains unexecuted and physically unvalidated.
candidates.changes: Specified interfaces and substitution slots; defined bounded loss and factorial sign; replaced impossible dual budget matching with primary cost and separate auxiliary designs; added type-only controls and independent builds.

candidates.title: Exception-aware failure memory without hidden-label access

sources.use: Transfer trajectory novelty to workflow search.
sources.boundary: Novelty is observer dependent.

sources.use: Graph-path hypothesis construction.
sources.boundary: Graph paths do not validate properties.

candidates.mechanism: Transfer ASAL historical-neighbor novelty to graph-path exploration. Evaluated failures store public path features, returned categories and context. Candidate novelty is minimum weighted Jaccard distance from stored public feature sets; candidate failure labels are unavailable. Rank by novelty times an online validity estimate trained only on observed outcomes. Selected plans always face unchanged oracle checks.
candidates.hypothesis: Failure-context memory may reduce invalid repetition beyond exact deduplication and failure counts without suppressing valid exceptions. Novelty and evidence validity remain separately measured.
candidates.experiment: Publish graph generator, deterministic oracle, signature vocabulary and equal feature weights before testing. Oracle labels appear only after charged queries. Include unit mismatch, unsupported edges and context-conditional incompatibility with rule-reversing exceptions. Mark 10% of training feedback uncertain, represented as unknown rather than hard failures. Reserve graphs and context-rule combinations; run thirty independent paired graph/search builds.
candidates.baseline: Compare success-only memory, exact executable-consequence deduplication, failure-count heuristics and online constraint learning using identical public features and observed labels. Match candidate generators and total cost: proposal, repair or archive query 1; oracle query 20. Count classifier updates and archive scans, reporting raw counts and wall time.
candidates.metric: Predeclare distinct valid consequences per cost, repeated failures, false rejection of exception plans and validity calibration. Evaluation-only exhaustive enumeration supplies equivalence labels; search cannot access those labels or unevaluated oracle outcomes. Resample independent graph builds for intervals.
candidates.falsifier: No added support if deduplication or constraint learning matches valid-plan yield, or novelty suppresses context reversals. Requiring hidden failure labels in candidate features invalidates the run rather than supporting memory.
candidates.confound: Handwritten signatures may encode intended generalization. Freeze features, oracle and reversals before holdouts; include unseen combinations and report uncertain labels separately. Public features may proxy rules, requiring feature-ablation controls.
candidates.feasibility: Hundreds of nodes and explicit constraints fit an offline CPU benchmark. Release code and split hashes before execution. This tests negative-result memory, not demonstrated materials discovery; no outcomes are asserted.
candidates.changes: Defined observable-only failure distance, ranking and uncertain feedback; prohibited label and equivalence-oracle leakage; added reversals, constraint-learning control, full costs and independent graph replicates.

candidates.title: Fair cost-niche selection against budget-aware Pareto archives

sources.use: Behavioral niches and local competition.
sources.boundary: No open-endedness guarantee.

sources.use: Graph-path hypothesis construction.
sources.boundary: Graph paths do not validate properties.

candidates.mechanism: Transfer Lenia local competition to graph-grounded plans. Freeze cost bins [1,2], [3,5], [6,10] and discrimination bins from training quartiles of d_mn=sum_P (mu_m-mu_n)^2/(2 sigma^2). Retain highest training identification accuracy per cell, capacity twelve. Every archive retrieves the feasible retained plan with highest training accuracy, ties by lower cost then immutable ID.
candidates.hypothesis: Cost niches may improve budget-conditioned accuracy over global top-k. Incremental benefit over same-capacity Pareto retention is separate; equal Pareto performance does not invalidate meaningful cost-conditioned coverage.
candidates.experiment: Use F=kx, F=kx+ax^3 and F=kx+a max(0,x-x0), positive parameters; displacement noise N(0,0.01^2); finite load plans from {0.1,0.3,0.6,1}. Cost sums public measurement costs; training accuracy and discrimination determine retention. Reserve topology generators, parameters and noise. Build thirty independent paired archives with the same pools and seeds. Test budgets {2,5,10} and a frozen shifted schedule doubling one measurement type’s cost.
candidates.baseline: Niche, top-k, Pareto and random archives each hold twelve plans and receive identical evaluated candidates, costs, feasible options and budget information. All use the same retrieval rule. Truncate oversized Pareto fronts by training-only crowding distance with deterministic ties. Charge enumeration, simulation, updates and storage; report search costs separately from deployment measurements.
candidates.metric: Report each budget’s accuracy and trapezoidal accuracy-budget area, with paired intervals across independent builds. Infeasible or empty choices score zero; report frequency. Separate contrasts versus top-k and Pareto, retaining negative results. Coverage is descriptive, not a success metric.
candidates.falsifier: No operational top-k superiority if the paired accuracy-area interval fails to exceed the prespecified meaningful gain of 0.02. Apply the same criterion separately to Pareto. Neither failure disproves the broader archive concept.
candidates.confound: Bins, costs and retrieval may privilege niches. Freeze all on training data and reveal identical budget information. Under shifted costs, recompute feasibility using the same frozen retrieval. Never inspect test accuracy for ties, truncation or plan selection.
candidates.feasibility: Scalar spring simulations and enumeration run offline on CPU. Training cost, storage and test measurements stay separate because they lack a natural common unit. All plans and performance comparisons remain untested.
candidates.changes: Fixed bins, capacity, descriptors and common budget-aware retrieval; matched candidate information and Pareto truncation; separated top-k/Pareto claims; added independent builds, shifted costs and overhead accounting.

evaluations.feedback: The illumination-to-response transfer is explicit and the graph analogy remains bounded. Positive spring stiffness alone does not ensure a nonsingular constrained network. Response classes and held-out evaluation geometry remain underspecified, making apparent descriptor success vulnerable to stiffness normalization and evaluator design.
evaluations.revision: Define node placement, connectivity, constraints and a rank rejection rule. Freeze a held-out response vector and class thresholds before selection; include graph-path-shuffled descriptor choices to test whether graph guidance contributes.

evaluations.feedback: The typed representation has a plausible executable boundary and a good induced-mutation confound control. However, the grammar and starting viable pattern are absent, so sixty mutations may mostly test initialization failure. Source transfer supports representation design, not the promised retention benefit.
evaluations.revision: Provide one viable two-channel seed, the exact graph-to-kernel compiler and clipping rules. Predefine viability, coefficient-change matching and failure handling; distinguish grammar constraints from explanatory labels in an ablation.

evaluations.feedback: ASAL Appendix B explicitly supports asymmetric typed-particle interactions; active driving is correctly distinguished from passive mechanics. The resource sensing law and tracking target are undefined. Matching coefficient bounds does not match realized actuation or isolate resource-driven motion from interspecies asymmetry.
evaluations.revision: Write the force and resource-sensing equations, force saturation and timestep. Compare symmetric and asymmetric laws under realized-force or work strata, with a resource-only controller and matched counterfactual displacement trials.

evaluations.feedback: The proposal responsibly labels new mechanochemical equations as assumptions. Yet the cited Lenia statistical measures do little mechanistic work, and the activator-inhibitor law, drive and strain feedback signs are missing. A ring of central springs may introduce floppy modes obscuring recovery.
evaluations.revision: Specify the complete reaction equations, coupling signs and ring stabilization. State the borrowed Lenia measure exactly and separate traveling-pulse recovery from externally driven oscillations using fixed-drive and fixed-geometry controls.

evaluations.feedback: The history-state intervention is promising, but MECHGPT Section 2.3.3 demonstrates DFT-based O2 force-field fitting, not viscoelastic constitutive identification. Passive rest-length adaptation and geometry-matched history separation require an explicit energy law; equal impulse alone does not equal work.
evaluations.revision: Relabel MECHGPT transfer as executable fitting workflow inspiration. Supply energy and dissipative evolution equations, pulse directions and geometry-matching procedure; verify nonnegative dissipation and avoid matching work by conditioning on post-treatment outcomes.

evaluations.feedback: The hidden-channel swap cleanly distinguishes visible geometry from an imposed historical state, with appropriate scalar-excitability controls. This tests programmed history dependence rather than discovery of memory, which is explicitly acknowledged. The growth law and physically attainable swapped-state constraints still need specification.
evaluations.revision: Publish the full visible-channel update and clipping. Separate reachable-history pairs from artificial swaps, preregister delay scaling and effect size, and compare localized history maps with equal-mean and equal-variance controls.

evaluations.feedback: Transferring local niche competition to lesion robustness is faithful without claiming regeneration. Held-out lesions and matched removed mass are useful. However, recovery can mean returning to any high-mass blob rather than preserving the original localized dynamics, and seed viability is assumed.
evaluations.revision: Name a reproducible viable seed and dynamics. Define functional recovery using localization, trajectory and persistence thresholds alongside mass; hold out lesion shape families and initial phases rather than only masks.

evaluations.feedback: The renderer-only intervention is a strong test of observer dependence and preserves the possibility that visual dynamics matter. Handcrafted descriptors cannot evaluate ASAL foundation-model performance, correctly noted. Candidate viability and perturbation definitions are still needed for a reproducible functional advantage test.
evaluations.revision: Freeze candidate generation, renderer transformations and perturbation-response vectors. Report both fixed-pool selection and search-loop versions separately, and include response-descriptor corruption to test whether gains depend on accurate functional measurements.

evaluations.feedback: The review-to-communication transfer is bounded and the provenance ablation targets a real causal alternative. Rule-based agents receiving free-form packets require a specified parser; otherwise differences may simply reflect unequal interpretability. Correlated sensors can remain dependent even with distinct provenance identifiers.
evaluations.revision: Use an identical parser or reversible packet encoding across conditions. Model shared sensor causes separately from duplicated relays, and preregister aggregation weights so provenance identity is not equated with statistical independence.

evaluations.feedback: ASAL motivates trajectory descriptors, but MECHGPT does not establish relative-coordinate swarm features; this is an engineering analogy. Resource transfer rules and archive-to-test policy selection are unspecified. Prerecorded embeddings may be invalid for newly generated policies unless the candidate pool is fixed.
evaluations.revision: Fix and cache one candidate-policy pool, specify exchange dynamics and archive retrieval, and describe MECHGPT as graph-interpretability inspiration. Compare pixel and fixed pretrained descriptors separately with all rendering and embedding costs recorded.

evaluations.feedback: The contradiction-triggered sensor intervention is specific, readily simulated and appropriately predicts a common-mode failure boundary. Equal-sampling controls and random resampling make it falsifiable. The current wording still leaves quorum thresholds, stopping rules and allocation of unused challenge tokens open.
evaluations.revision: Provide the finite-state protocol, token budget and quorum rule. Match sequential stopping and sample timing across controls, then report a preregistered delay-error frontier over localized and common-mode failure rates.

evaluations.feedback: The source-combination routing mechanism is explicit and does not mistake graph paths for physical laws. However, a parity task makes source complementarity nearly definitional; novelty may reduce to collecting missing bits. Packet payload growth and reducer access could dominate routing comparisons.
evaluations.revision: Define per-packet bits, route termination and aggregation. Add a greedy missing-source coverage baseline, tasks with redundant or irrelevant sources, and separate benefits of historical novelty from source-aware routing information.

evaluations.feedback: Archive retention and graph-indexed reuse are transferred coherently to collective adaptation. The dominant effect could be an external controller retrieving entire policies rather than population memory. Recurring regimes also create a legitimate memorization benefit, so recurrence alone should not be treated as failure.
evaluations.revision: Specify whether memory and retrieval are local or centralized. Separate recurring-regime reuse from unseen-regime transfer, include a matched centralized library control, and define recovery thresholds independently of observed results.

evaluations.feedback: Ancestry tracking gives a concrete mechanism and a strong simpler-memory falsifier. The papers supply motivation rather than proof, correctly bounded. The correction oracle and source-disproof semantics are idealizations: one false observation does not normally invalidate every claim from its source.
evaluations.revision: Distinguish correction of one observation from revocation of source reliability. Define probabilistic discount rules and test false corrections, missing links and independent corroboration while keeping correction arrival times identical.

evaluations.feedback: Team-level selection and role ablations operationalize complementarity beyond labels. Yet removing signalers also changes population and resource budgets; equalizing sensing could erase the very specialization being tested. The mechanism needs explicit action costs and a functional replacement control.
evaluations.revision: Define role policies and action budgets. Replace removed signalers with matched-cost nonsignaling agents, hold total population fixed, and compare archive benefits against reward-only team search under identical visibility distributions.

evaluations.feedback: The selection niche fits, but consensus validity, fault assumptions and mixed-policy composition are underspecified. MECHGPT Section 2.3 concerns LLM teams executing materials tasks, not validation of fault-tolerant consensus. Adaptive mixtures can fail even when each constituent protocol works separately.
evaluations.revision: State topology, synchrony, fault budget and a feasible consensus objective. Specify a composable switching protocol, retain identical detectors across baselines, and present MECHGPT only as executable-agent-workflow inspiration.

evaluations.feedback: Adaptive behavioral descriptors and grounded retrieval are cleanly transferred, with sensible template holdouts and fixed-category reporting. But learned descriptors from only fifty cards can be unstable, and minimum-template accuracy requires a declared rule choosing a workflow from the archive without labels.
evaluations.revision: Specify descriptor learning, training sample count and query-time archive selection without answer access. Add a fixed-descriptor archive baseline and report uncertainty over held-out template families rather than only question instances.

evaluations.feedback: Counterfactual discrimination is an explicit workflow behavior descriptor, with meaningful misspecification and information-gain controls. Three linear spring laws may be indistinguishable under the chosen interventions. Hidden-law accuracy must not reward arbitrary labels for observationally equivalent models or omit unknown-model calibration.
evaluations.revision: List constitutive laws, admissible loads and noise. Verify identifiability before training, score equivalent laws together, and predefine unknown-model detection thresholds with calibration and abstention penalties on the withheld fourth law.

evaluations.feedback: Typed recombination and the two-substitution factorial contrast make module interaction testable rather than metaphorical. Lenia supplies evolutionary variation and retention, not evidence for workflow crossover. Matching both attempted children and solver calls needs explicit accounting because compatibility rejection changes execution rates.
evaluations.revision: Define module interfaces, two chosen substitution slots and accuracy loss. Report attempted-child and solver-budget experiments separately; include type-only screening and assumption-aware screening to isolate scientific compatibility from syntax filtering.

evaluations.feedback: Evidence-dependent plan value is a credible interaction mechanism, and the bookkeeping-only ablation is essential. The Bayesian or heuristic update rule remains unspecified, so true-model probability and preservation of alternatives are not reproducible metrics yet. ASAL is search inspiration, not evidence for coupling benefits.
evaluations.revision: Provide likelihoods, ledger semantics and reprioritization equations. Split deduplication, evidence conditioning and archive retention into factorial controls; evaluate posterior calibration and unknown-law abstention alongside identification accuracy under misspecification.

evaluations.feedback: The failure-signature memory implements a clear historical influence and directly challenges the deduplication alternative. The synthetic oracle keeps feasibility high but can build the desired generalization into hand-authored categories. Validity and novelty should stay separate when uncertain failures generalize poorly.
evaluations.revision: Publish failure signatures and proposal scoring before held-out graphs. Include context reversals and uncertain failure labels, compare a constraint-learning baseline, and charge all repairs, archive queries and oracle evaluations consistently.

evaluations.feedback: The archive-to-reusable-routine transfer is explicit and correctly bounded to workflow memory. Provenance-matched controls isolate some benefits, but the assembly procedure and applicability checker are absent. Counting routines independently needs behavior-based equivalence, otherwise renamed templates can inflate archive diversity.
evaluations.revision: Define routine signatures, applicability tests and assembly search. Freeze behavioral equivalence on held-out input probes; separate diversity retention, provenance checks and reuse using a factorial design with all validation costs charged.

evaluations.feedback: Cost-conditioned local selection is an especially clear QD transfer and includes a serious Pareto-front alternative. The retrieval rule and cost-to-information tradeoff need precise definitions. Rejection against Pareto performance concerns added value, not whether cost-conditioned archives are scientifically meaningful.
evaluations.revision: Specify cost bins, discrimination descriptors and budget-time selection. Match feasible candidate sets across methods, report uncertainty per budget and distinguish superiority over top-k from incremental value beyond Pareto retention.

evaluations.feedback: Redescription invariance yields an explicit selection test with an appropriate consequence-deduplication baseline. Its relation to ASAL is an extension, not a reported result. Synthetic oracle consequences can make success circular unless evaluators are frozen and independently separate the selection and testing contexts.
evaluations.revision: Publish equivalence labels, context fields and abstention rules. Hold out intervention families and transformation generators, and compare consequence-only deduplication under identical oracle access, reporting valid distinctions lost through invariance filtering.

evaluations.feedback: Geometry, rank screening, independent loads and graph-shuffling now make the representation transfer reproducible. Fixed-pool scope is appropriately bounded. However, the 200-attempt cap may produce fewer than 100 accepted motifs; confidence intervals spanning zero indicate inconclusive advantage rather than evidence of absence.
evaluations.revision: Specify minimum accepted pool size and handling of cap failures without selective replacement. Distinguish an equivalence test from an inconclusive superiority test, and report whether the four proposed classes are actually populated.

evaluations.feedback: Explicit active equations, held-out jumps and search-level replication address the main causal gaps. The resource-only control still retains the repulsive force when pair coefficients are zero, so its label is inaccurate. Work strata are properly acknowledged as diagnostics, not randomized energy matching.
evaluations.revision: Call zero-coefficient control resource-plus-repulsion, or remove the entire pair term for a true resource-only arm. Define zero-distance unit vectors and report matched-time work-performance frontiers without interpreting post-outcome strata causally.

evaluations.feedback: The full update, reachable-state distinction and reset controls meaningfully improve causal interpretation. The imposed 0.95 hidden-state decay applies exactly only when visible trajectories remain matched throughout, not merely at intervention time. Candidate disks may extinguish; reporting extinction protects against selective survivor claims.
evaluations.revision: Derive hidden-state differences with the visible-input difference term included, or clamp visible trajectories for the exponential benchmark. Preregister handling of zero initial or extinct mass, and label useful-memory claims separately from programmed sensitivity.

evaluations.feedback: The revision sharply separates handcrafted rendering from ASAL performance and fixes whole-family holdouts. Failure-only diversity is controlled. Viability conditioning can still select different survivor populations across arms, and a pool with fewer than ten viable candidates needs an explicit archive policy.
evaluations.revision: Define archive eligibility and shortfall handling before selecting ten elites. Report an intention-to-select outcome charging extinct candidates alongside survivor-only distances, and state exactly which frames and normalization constants enter image descriptors.

evaluations.feedback: Equal parsing and separate provenance switches directly address representation fairness; correlated origins are no longer mistaken for independence. However, relation compatibility and uncertainty fields remain undefined in a hidden-bit task. Without an explicit relation algebra, the hypothesized typing effect cannot be reproduced.
evaluations.revision: Define packet field widths, sensor generative laws and relation compatibility table. Fix how incompatible reports are weighted and predeclare the incremental typing contrast separately from provenance and uncertainty contributions.

evaluations.feedback: Fixed times, sample budgets and failure-family holdouts substantially tighten the intervention. The sources remain motivation rather than validation. The most recently disagreeing pair is not uniquely defined when reports change simultaneously, and final quorum decisions need explicit failure or abstention scoring.
evaluations.revision: Specify deterministic pair tie-breaking, whether a resample replaces or augments each vote, and scores for no quorum. Report sample-allocation effects separately from message protocol effects under the shared bit ceiling.

evaluations.feedback: Claim-specific corrections, fallible reliability and observation-ID controls repair the earlier source-revocation issue. The ancestry advantage now faces a credible simpler baseline. Frozen likelihood contributions still need a rule for dependent original observations, otherwise calibration can fail despite perfect relay deduplication.
evaluations.revision: Specify the likelihood combination and correction-discount equations, including common-cause handling. Test independent duplicates, correlated originals and false corrections separately; report the graph storage tradeoff against flat observation-ID memory at each byte budget.

evaluations.feedback: Matched population replacement and shuffled messages now test information value rather than simple agent removal. Identical sensing and costs bound the role claim appropriately. The policy grammar and archive descriptor remain verbal, and per-recipient broadcast charging must reconcile sender actions with transmission energy.
evaluations.revision: Publish finite-state transition tables, descriptor bins and mutation probabilities. Define simultaneous sensing and actions plus exact broadcast accounting, then preregister role replacement contrasts and independent search count before evaluating unseen maps.

evaluations.feedback: Concrete laws, explicit noise, unknown-model calibration and independent archives repair major identifiability gaps. The discrimination descriptor is a justified extension, not a source result. Pairwise closeness within five sigma is not transitive, so equivalence-class merging needs a mathematically specified grouping rule.
evaluations.revision: Define equivalence classes using a conservative complete-link criterion or score response-distance tolerance directly. Publish parameter priors and plan composition, and separate threshold calibration from fourth-law distinguishability evaluation without test-label access.

evaluations.feedback: The factorial sign, invalid-workflow penalty and separate budget designs now make the interaction claim auditable. Source boundaries are precise. Clipping can create apparent nonadditivity near the loss ceiling, while weighted accounting units remain an operational convention rather than equal compute.
evaluations.revision: Report unclipped errors for valid workflows alongside bounded loss and validity transitions. Freeze module implementations and timing calibration, and show interaction signs across cost weights and alternative scientifically interpretable loss scales.

evaluations.feedback: Observable-only candidate features and exception tests address leakage. One inconsistency remains: the baseline promises exact executable-consequence deduplication while equivalence labels are evaluation-only. Without a public computable equality test, either the baseline gets privileged information or its promised comparison cannot be implemented.
evaluations.revision: Use canonical executable serialization or public probe-signature deduplication as the search baseline; reserve exact oracle consequence equivalence for evaluation. Specify the online validity estimator, update budget and scoring treatment of uncertain feedback.

evaluations.feedback: Common retrieval rules and separate Pareto claims address the strongest fairness concerns. Four quartile bins for three pair distances crossed with three cost bins can create far more than twelve cells. Capacity twelve therefore requires an eviction rule that may undo local niche competition.
evaluations.revision: Define twelve cells explicitly or publish a deterministic training-only eviction policy shared with appropriate controls. Specify measurement costs and nonlinear parameter priors, then report occupied cells and eviction-induced losses without consulting held-out accuracy.

evaluations.feedback: The fixed candidate pool isolates descriptor choice cleanly, and withheld loads are a useful external test. Disconnected motifs can remain singular despite fixed boundaries; repeated pools, independent response-class definitions and a prespecified distance normalization are still missing.
evaluations.revision: Declare connectivity and rank checks, two training loads, disjoint evaluation angles and twenty independent motif pools. Freeze normalization and compare archives within each pool, reporting paired uncertainty across pools.

evaluations.feedback: Matched coefficient-change distributions are the right control, but sixty mutations and one withheld seed do not establish robustness across search runs. Grammar-versus-flat differences can disappear once both encode the same induced proposal distribution; that null result must remain informative.
evaluations.revision: Publish the grammar compiler and growth equation; freeze viability thresholds. Run multiple independent searches and evaluate each retained archive on a reserved seed bank, matching coefficient-change distributions and full rollout cost.

evaluations.feedback: The displaced-resource intervention makes pursuit testable, with force-strength accounting appropriately explicit. However, equal force magnitude is not equal actuation work, and the reciprocal search has fewer free parameters. Search and holdout seeds must be separated before coefficient selection.
evaluations.revision: Specify interaction kernels, integrator and resource sensing; compare matched effective search budgets and realized work. Reserve independent resource trajectories and seeds, using coefficient-search runs as replication units rather than particle counts.

evaluations.feedback: The intervention and timestep check are sensible, but no activator-inhibitor equations or bounded rest-length law are actually supplied. Establishing a stable traveling pulse and mechanical coupling within one day is optimistic; equal integration calls also need to include refinement costs.
evaluations.revision: Start with one published or fully specified excitable-ring equation and verify its uncoupled pulse. Freeze coupling and indentation grids, reserve disturbance phases, and compare independently initialized rings with refinement costs explicitly charged.

evaluations.feedback: Equal impulse does not imply equal work, while equal work and exactly matched visible geometry may be difficult to realize for different histories. The claimed passive internal-variable energy is unnamed. Noisy repeats of one motif support only within-motif memory discrimination.
evaluations.revision: Write the energy and relaxation dynamics and derive dissipation first. Define geometry-matching tolerance without selecting on outcome, hold out pulse amplitudes, and distinguish independent motif replicates from repeated noisy observations of one motif.

evaluations.feedback: The hidden-state swap is a direct, inexpensive causal test with an explicit update and appropriate scalar-gain controls. Because memory is built into the equations, a positive result verifies implementation and state dependence; it cannot establish newly evolved memory or general utility.
evaluations.revision: Freeze the visible growth rule, probe and mass-response window. Pair every history with reset, mean-only and shuffled-state interventions; hold out pulse intervals and report paired effects across independently initialized patterns.

evaluations.feedback: The proposal has clear selection and held-out lesion tests, but identical mutation streams cannot generally persist after selection chooses different parents. Eighty candidates near one viable seed may characterize that lineage rather than a transferable recovery-selection effect.
evaluations.revision: Pair random-number schedules rather than requiring identical offspring. Run independent searches from several viable seeds, separate search and evaluation rollouts, freeze mass-matched lesion operators, and summarize recovery per search archive.

evaluations.feedback: Renderer-only perturbations provide a particularly sharp negative control, and the shared candidate pool cleanly tests selection. Response novelty may nevertheless overfit its handcrafted assays, while a simple silhouette descriptor would be an unfair proxy for ASAL foundation-model descriptors.
evaluations.revision: State that visual baselines are handcrafted, freeze all descriptors and function assays, hold out entire perturbation families, and replicate shared candidate pools. Include untreated persistence so selecting diverse failure responses cannot win.

evaluations.feedback: The synthetic packet test is executable and addresses duplicated evidence directly. Typed formatting bundles provenance, uncertainty and compatibility rules, so its apparent benefit may be entirely source deduplication. Message-count matching alone does not guarantee equal bits or aggregation access.
evaluations.revision: Specify the packet schema, Bayesian reference aggregator and equal bit budget. Factorially ablate provenance, typing and uncertainty; reserve sensor-reliability distributions and duplicate rates, reporting error and calibration across independent simulated worlds.

evaluations.feedback: Translation controls and anchored-resource counterexamples are valuable, but the forager policy family, transfer rules and image embedding implementation remain unspecified. An independent ensemble is not obviously a valid comparator for a task that requires resource exchange, complicating fair-budget interpretation.
evaluations.revision: Define a small deterministic grid-world and finite policy catalogue first. Compare graph, matched low-cost image and random archives on identical policies; reserve map generators and score independent archive-building runs at fixed simulator budgets.

evaluations.feedback: Contradiction-triggered sampling is a concrete interaction mechanism with a useful common-mode-failure counterprediction. The fresh-sample allocation can accidentally change observation budgets or timing. Shared failure episodes, rather than individual reports, must define independent replicates and train-test separation.
evaluations.revision: Specify quorum, contradiction threshold and sample ledger. Give every policy identical pre-generated sample streams and total observation/message ceilings; reserve failure-pattern families and report episode-level paired error-delay tradeoffs including common-mode cases.

evaluations.feedback: Parity makes complementary information objectively testable, but an independent ensemble with centralized aggregation could solve the puzzle without meaningful routing constraints. Equal received packets can also hide different transmission costs, and prelabelled relevant sources may trivialize novelty selection.
evaluations.revision: Specify observation and aggregator locality, packet size and per-edge transmission costs. Compare source-aware random routing and fixed shortest paths; withhold graph families and sensor allocations, evaluating independent evolved routing policies rather than packets.

evaluations.feedback: The recurring-versus-unprecedented shift comparison cleanly distinguishes reuse from general adaptation. However, a minority policy is not yet operationally defined, and the retrieval mechanism may carry most of the benefit. Equal slots need matching policy complexity as well as counts.
evaluations.revision: Freeze graph descriptors, niche thresholds and an observation-only retrieval rule. Cross archive-retention and retrieval ablations under equal memory bytes, train on separate maps, and report adaptation across independently generated regime sequences.

evaluations.feedback: Packet replay is inexpensive and directly exercises ancestry memory; corrupt-link stress tests are especially important. A ground-truth correction delivered to every agent is stronger information than realistic corroboration, so reversal speed alone may reward mechanically trusting a privileged correction channel.
evaluations.revision: Add unreliable corrections with known calibrated reliability and a source-ID deduplication baseline. Freeze discount rules before testing, reserve graph and corruption families, and pair outcomes by independent report-cascade episode.

evaluations.feedback: Role removal makes complementarity testable, but simply deleting signalers also reduces population size and action budget. Training sparse and testing dense visibility mainly tests loss of usefulness; it does not alone show improved generalization to new coordination challenges.
evaluations.revision: Replace removed signalers with equal-cost neutral or alternate-role agents, not empty slots. Freeze policy grammars and capacities; evaluate independent searches on unseen sparse maps as well as dense visibility controls and matched team sizes.

evaluations.feedback: Fault-niche selection is plausible, but a mixed consensus population can violate convergence even when each homogeneous policy converges. Switching rules and adversarial corruption assumptions are unspecified. Building and validating that protocol library is a larger task than the stated easy CPU feasibility suggests.
evaluations.revision: Choose a bounded finite-state consensus protocol family with explicit fault thresholds and mixing semantics. Validate homogeneous baselines first, freeze detector and switching rules, then evaluate independent graph instances and withheld fault-switch schedules.

evaluations.feedback: The authored evidence corpus makes support labels cheap and budgets inspectable. Fifty cards and exact claim keys can nevertheless turn retrieval into template matching; learned descriptor adaptation requires a training-only fitting rule, and worst-template performance may be unstable with tiny test groups.
evaluations.revision: Publish corpus generation, retrieval configurations and descriptor-fitting code. Reserve relation families and question generators, keep test answers inaccessible during fitting, and report per-family sample counts with paired independent corpus/search replications.

evaluations.feedback: Counterfactual model discrimination gives a clear external task, and the unknown-law test addresses misspecification. The descriptor still needs a formula and uncertainty model. An expected-information baseline given the same correct toy laws may be hard to beat, appropriately limiting ambitious claims.
evaluations.revision: Specify measurement distributions, discrimination distance and unknown-model rejection threshold using training data. Reserve topology generators and law parameters; compare independent search archives at matched total forward-solve and measurement costs, retaining negative results.

evaluations.feedback: The single-substitution factorial is an unusually useful check on claimed workflow synergy. Equal attempted children and solver calls cannot generally both be fixed when compatibility screening rejects different fractions; curated module traps may also favor the proposed type system.
evaluations.revision: Choose one primary total-cost budget and report attempted children and solver calls separately. Publish a fixed module library, reserve assumption-error families, and estimate interaction contrasts within matched problems across independent workflow-search runs.

evaluations.feedback: The shared evidence ledger supports an executable interaction test, but repeated noisy measurements are not necessarily duplicates: they can be informative replication. Deleting all repeats from baselines could cripple legitimate uncertainty reduction, while true-model retention needs an explicit probabilistic update rule.
evaluations.revision: Define duplicates as exact reused observations, separately price independent repeated measurements, and supply likelihood/update equations. Reserve law parameters and noise regimes; compare independent policy-search runs including misspecified-law rejection and calibrated uncertainty.

evaluations.feedback: A deterministic graph oracle makes the proposed negative-memory mechanism readily testable. However, novelty distance over failure signatures is undefined, and repeated evaluation within one graph is not independent replication. Context-dependent exceptions are essential to distinguish learning from simply blacklisting categories.
evaluations.revision: Publish the oracle, failure-distance function and exception generator. Reserve graph instances and context-rule combinations, charge every constraint query, and compare paired independent searches against failure-count heuristics and exact executable-consequence deduplication.

evaluations.feedback: Lineage-preserving routine reuse has a manageable implementation path, with good template holdouts and overhead accounting. The no-memory baseline cannot literally share library capacity, and solver calls may be a poor cost proxy when cached routines do substantial non-solver computation.
evaluations.revision: Specify routine contracts, frozen retrieval and provenance validators. Match memory-enabled baselines by bytes, report cold-start and amortized costs separately, and reserve complete task-generating templates while pairing independent library construction and evaluation runs.

evaluations.feedback: Budget-specific accuracy and a Pareto comparator make the hypothesis falsifiable without equating diversity with quality. The retrieval rule could itself give the niche archive privileged budget conditioning; paired measurement noise and archive capacity need precise accounting across methods.
evaluations.revision: Use one train-only retrieval rule applicable to every archive, with identical budget information and plan costs. Freeze budget bins and shifted-cost tests, and report paired independent archive builds with full enumeration and storage overhead.

evaluations.feedback: Known consequence labels and explicit paraphrase controls support a compact selection test. Forty authored directions may reveal evaluator design rather than scientific generalization, and consequence-equivalence queries can leak the oracle solution if they share labels with the final evaluation.

Reserve consequence-generating rules and contextual transformations, audit false merges, and compare independently generated corpora against consequence-only deduplication at matched query and storage budgets.

evaluations.feedback: The geometry, rank rejection, fixed normalization and twenty independent pools now make this a directly executable descriptor comparison. The attempt cap may produce undersized pools, and the four-class outcome could collapse to one class under these load and boundary choices.
evaluations.revision: Prespecify treatment of pools with fewer than one hundred accepted motifs; never silently refill differently across methods. Check class occupancy using calibration-only motifs and report continuous held-out distances even when class coverage degenerates.

evaluations.feedback: The force law, sensing-frozen control and search-level uncertainty substantially improve identifiability of the proposed effect. Reciprocal coefficients at fixed off-diagonal norm have only two distinct possibilities, so twenty-four evaluations may mostly repeat candidates while asymmetry receives genuine exploration.
evaluations.revision: Enumerate the reciprocal family exactly and report its two-point support. Separate simulator-cost parity from distinct-proposal counts; add an equal-dimensional reciprocal control by varying another declared interaction parameter without changing force or sensing budgets.

evaluations.feedback: This is now an executable programmed-memory intervention with clear paired controls and an honest distinction between artificial swaps and reachable histories. Extinction and clipping may eliminate useful probe responses; recording them prevents success-biased filtering but cannot rescue an uninformative dynamical regime.
evaluations.revision: Freeze zero-distance unit conventions, FFT convolution and state-matching procedures. Report all twenty initializations and reachable-match rates; if responses vanish, conclude the specified regime is uninformative rather than tuning on held-out pulse intervals.

evaluations.feedback: The frozen sampler, renderers, viability screen and held-out intervention families make the comparison materially stronger. Fixed-coordinate training lesions may hit empty space for many localized seeds, creating zero response vectors; differing viable counts can also destabilize pairwise-diversity estimates.
evaluations.revision: Prespecify zero-occupancy assays and archives with fewer than two viable survivors. Report overlap mass for every intervention and coverage alongside conditional pairwise diversity, without moving lesions after inspecting held-out outcomes.

evaluations.feedback: The factorial design now separates typing from provenance and uncertainty, while equal bits and inaccessible oracle parameters address major fairness concerns. The exact relation-compatibility semantics and aggregation equations remain unspecified, so implementation choices could still determine whether typing has any independent content.
evaluations.revision: Publish relation truth tables, bit allocations, uncertainty quantization and all eight aggregators before sampling test worlds. Fix episode counts and a shared initial-information rule, keeping the Bayesian oracle strictly outside policy tuning and archive selection.

evaluations.feedback: The explicit deadlines, sample ledger and held-out failure families make the protocol comparison credible. The rule selecting the most recently disagreeing pair needs deterministic tie handling, and it is unclear whether updated votes replace previous samples or combine all observations.
evaluations.revision: Define pair selection, cyclic ordering and vote updates exactly; resolve disagreement ties by immutable sensor IDs. Publish the failure generators and independent episode count, then compare complete error-abstention-delay curves rather than selecting one favorable threshold afterward.

evaluations.feedback: Fallible claim-specific corrections, flat observation-ID memory and equal-byte controls now isolate ancestry storage more convincingly. Likelihood weighting still requires explicit dependence assumptions; correlated distinct-source claims can remain overcounted even with perfect relay deduplication and calibrated correction reliability.
evaluations.revision: Release the likelihood equations, graph encoding and retention policy with fixed byte costs. Distinguish error from incorrect correlation assumptions from error due to corrupted ancestry, and report performance separately across held-out common-cause and correction-shift regimes.

evaluations.feedback: Equal-cost role replacement and dummy-location controls directly address the previous deletion confound. Execution is still less specified than the small packet benchmarks: role transition rules, map sizes, search-run count and how receiver energy is charged remain open implementation decisions.
evaluations.revision: Publish complete finite-state transitions, map generator, action scheduling and sender/receiver energy ledger. Fix independent search count and evaluation allocation; report replacement and dummy-message effects per frozen team across shared held-out maps.

evaluations.feedback: Explicit laws, noise, counterfactual descriptors and unknown-law calibration make the benchmark testable. Approximate response closeness is not transitive, so calling merged models equivalence classes requires a clustering rule. Parallel-spring topologies may also be observationally identical beyond their summed parameters.
evaluations.revision: Freeze a transitive clustering procedure or score pairwise distinguishability without classes. Audit effective network diversity and parameter identifiability using training-only generators, then report held-out topology cases that reduce to the same aggregate force-displacement law.

evaluations.feedback: The four-loss factorial contrast and separation of primary accounting from auxiliary budgets now identify the intended comparison. The numerical weights are declared, but describing them as both fixed constants and timing-calibrated quantities leaves an avoidable ambiguity about the actual stopping rule.
evaluations.revision: Choose either the stated fixed accounting weights or a preregistered calibration algorithm before testing. Publish executable module contracts, count all rejected children, and report raw operations, runtime and sensitivity to alternative weights alongside the primary result.

evaluations.feedback: Observable-only features, exception reversals and online-constraint controls substantially reduce leakage and trivial-blacklisting explanations. The experiment is small enough to execute, but the primary cost expression does not assign explicit weights to classifier updates and archive scans despite promising full accounting.
evaluations.revision: Freeze weights for updates and scanned entries, including empty-history novelty and cold-start validity priors. Keep uncertain feedback distinguishable from confirmed invalidity, and report ablations against constraint learning on the identical exposed feature and label stream.

The shifted cost schedule requires a precise split between archive retention and deployment retrieval, and the referenced spring laws are not supplied inside this standalone candidate.
